genre: short-form podcast / interview reel (vertical, 120s or less, Shorts children)

source.measured: frame-level breakdown of 28 owner-selected premium Instagram reference reels, Oct 2026 (phase-1 refs_* analysis and DESIGN_BRIEF)
source.note: references for craft relationships only; never copy their content, logos or identities

identity: One complete micro-story lifted from a longer conversation — a hook line, the setup it needs, a turn and a payoff — delivered as a DESIGNED short-form piece. The speaker owns a composed vertical frame; a typography and motion-graphics system carries the speech: hero words and graphics land on the spoken word. Zooms and sound effects are optional, never rules: restraint is the default, and each zoom or sound is reached for only when a specific moment needs it. A captioned plate with nothing designed on it is the failure mode, not the safe choice.

rules.story: keep one complete micro-story: open on its strongest intelligible line, keep the setup the payoff depends on, end on the resolved line or a deliberate cliff; never splice unrelated answers into a synthetic claim; cut dead time and repairable filler word-safely
rules.hook: the first second carries a pattern interrupt (a hook title or word slam on the first strong word, a card reveal, a flash) and the hook line is on screen within about 1.5s; a punch-in at 0s is an option, never a requirement; no fade from black
rules.frame: fill the vertical frame with the speaker (auto_reframe / focus_track per shot); no half-black or postage-stamp canvas; on two-person footage frame the active speaker
rules.camera: ZOOMS AND SOUND EFFECTS ARE OPTIONAL, NEVER RULES: a steady, well-framed picture is the default and zero zooms is a fine answer. Reach for a zoom only when a specific moment needs it — the word the story turns on, a reveal, a genuinely jarring jump cut — never one per cut, sentence, hold or hero moment; a bare jump cut is fine. When a move is earned, aim it at the face (add_zoom with measured cx/cy), ease it and vary it so it never reads as an automated pass
rules.typography: one designed type system: captions with a bold sans backbone and ONE accent role (keyword colour or italic serif) on 1-2 words per sentence, placed in face-free space above the platform UI band; hero words, numbers and names land as motion graphics on their spoken onset (add_motion_graphic — list_motion_templates), entrances short and graphic, exits faster than entrances
rules.motion_graphics: use the motion layer for the beats that carry the story: hook title, number counters, name/role labels, lists, social/UI cards, callouts; each graphic settles and holds still, never covers the face, and is silent unless the moment clearly earns one library sound
rules.sound: speech is the lead; no music unless the user supplied or asked for it (never chosen by the agent); sound effects are optional, never rules — zero is a fine answer — and come only from the approved library (list_sound_library, add_sfx storage_key='sound:<id>') where a specific on-screen moment earns one: a graphic landing (peak on the frame), a real section change or B-roll entry, the payoff, or a shown real-world action (shutter, typing, click, cash register); never on captions, ordinary cuts or as a sound per landing or transition; about one sound every 4-5 s at most (a ceiling, usually far fewer); a brief stop-down silence before a reveal
rules.transitions: hard cuts inside one take stay invisible; section turns, hook-to-body and B-roll entries may earn a whip/flash/zoom transition, with one library sound only when that turn earns it
rules.finish: one committed grade with light grain/texture; loudness mastered for social (set_master_loudness); the last frame loops cleanly into the first
